candidates.attacker_control: A user able to insert wiki/macro content controls both the body of the Raw macro and its mandatory syntax parameter. Selecting an HTML-family syntax makes the generated RawBlock eligible for direct HTML output.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: The Raw macro is explicitly designed to emit raw content, and the raw module is not part of the standalone distribution POM, so it may be considered trusted-only or omitted from some deployments. No code in this repository sets TransformationContext.restricted to true or calls setRestricted(true), so the in-repository caller that establishes the restricted security boundary was not found. The HTML macro's clean=false rejection and RESTRICTED cleaner parameter are direct evidence that the boundary is intended to be enforced by macros, but they do not prove platform reachability for RawMacro.
candidates.impact: Potential stored or reflected cross-site scripting when restricted-mode output is displayed in a user's browser. Injected HTML can include script or event-handler content that runs in the application origin, potentially performing actions as the victim or exposing page data. The issue also defeats an explicit security boundary intended to keep untrusted rendering safe.
candidates.prerequisites: The Raw macro module must be loaded and not separately disabled or permission-gated by the host; the macro transformation must process content with restricted mode enabled; rendering must target an HTML-family syntax. The attacker normally also needs permission to edit or submit the affected content.
candidates.root_cause: RawMacro.execute unconditionally creates a RawBlock from the macro body and the user-supplied syntax. It never checks MacroTransformationContext.getTransformationContext().isRestricted(), even though the rendering API defines restricted mode as the boundary at which potentially insecure macros such as HTML/script-producing macros must not execute. HTMLMacro implements that boundary, but the Raw macro is an equivalent raw-HTML path and omits the check.
candidates.title: Raw macro bypasses restricted rendering and emits attacker-controlled HTML
candidates.trace: Wiki/macro input -> parser creates a MacroBlock for the Raw macro -> MacroTransformation executes the selected macro without its own restricted-mode filter -> RawMacro creates new RawBlock(content, parameters.getSyntax()) -> block traversal reaches XHTMLChainingRenderer.onRawText -> because the supplied syntax is in SyntaxType.HTML_FAMILY_TYPES, XHTMLWikiPrinter.printRaw writes the body without XML escaping. A restricted caller therefore receives raw attacker HTML instead of the sanitized/blocked output it requested.
candidates.unverified: No build, test, or runtime rendering was performed. It is unverified whether the XWiki Platform distribution enables RawMacro for unprivileged editors, whether it always invokes restricted-mode rendering for their content, and whether any downstream platform filter sanitizes the rendered HTML despite the renderer's raw output.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation (XSS) / restricted-context bypass

coverage_summary: The source scope reported 749 model-visible files with no size-, sensitive-name-, or symlink-based exclusions; binary-like files are subject to read/search filtering. I inspected the module/POM layout and security-relevant code across the API, macros, syntax parsers/renderers, transformations, and XML modules, including restricted-context handling, raw/HTML output, reference parsing/URL handling, link checking, and XML parser configuration. I did not read all 749 files line-by-line. The P1 index is partial: 748 files indexed, 1 source file missing, 594 Java files parsed, 2 parse errors, 5,608 unresolved calls, and no control-flow, data-flow, semantic-resolution, runtime-reachability, or exploitability analysis. No build, tests, scanners, or exploit payloads were run.
limitations: The restricted-mode callers and XWiki Platform permission checks are outside this repository snapshot; the candidate is therefore a source-level lead, not a confirmed exploitable path.
No test sources were present in the assigned tree, and no runtime rendering or browser behavior was executed or confirmed.
The relation index omits one file, reports two parse errors, and has thousands of unresolved calls; unreported code paths were not treated as reviewed.
Host-level macro disabling, CSP, downstream HTML sanitization, and the default distribution's activation of the Raw macro remain unverified.
Binary-like files cannot be read or searched when a NUL byte is detected; no such exclusions were reported for this case, but the policy still applies.

rejected_leads.lead: javascript:// links accepted by URLResourceReferenceTypeParser and emitted as raw href by the XHTML link renderer
rejected_leads.reason: The generic URL parser deliberately permits unknown browser protocols and the link renderer is generic rather than a sanitizer; any host-level URL filtering or browser/CSP behavior was not verified. This is a plausible XSS lead but weaker than the explicit restricted-mode contract bypass.

rejected_leads.lead: Blind SSRF in the linkchecker transformation/DefaultHTTPChecker
rejected_leads.reason: LinkBlock URLs reach an Apache HttpClient GET without host/IP allowlisting, but the linkchecker module is optional and its transformation enablement, redirect policy, and real deployment exposure are not established in this snapshot. Only status codes are retained, making impact blind and configuration-dependent.

rejected_leads.lead: XXE or entity-expansion issues in XML/XHTML parsers
rejected_leads.reason: The primary parsers enable FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING and install a LocalEntityResolver, and no concrete bypass was found in the available source.

rejected_leads.lead: Arbitrary HTML attributes/event handlers from parser parameters reaching XHTMLChainingRenderer
rejected_leads.reason: The renderer copies parameter maps into HTML attributes, but whether untrusted wiki syntax can supply event-handler names and whether a host-level sanitizer runs afterward could not be established; this is a broad lead rather than a verified boundary violation.

summary: The strongest source-backed candidate is a restricted-rendering bypass in the Raw macro: unlike the HTML macro, it converts attacker-controlled content and an attacker-selected HTML-family syntax into a RawBlock without checking the restricted-context flag, and the XHTML renderer then writes that block without escaping. This is a plausible stored/reflected XSS path when a host renders untrusted content in restricted mode. No runtime execution, build, or platform-level reachability was verified.
